key_insight: Combining multi-scale foundation-model and FastVim features improved patch-level prostate Gleason grading over the best single-scale model.
clinical_relevance: This pathology AI approach could support more consistent prostate cancer grading, but it is not a drug-discovery method or a clinically validated tool.
method: Combine frozen pathology foundation-model features with raw-image features from a lightweight, distilled FastVim.
Use Mamba state-space models to encode spatial context at each scale.
Jointly train a fusion head to produce one patch-level grade prediction.
evidence_signal: On PANDA with 5-fold cross-validation, macro F1 reached 0.894 and Gleason pattern 5 F1 reached 0.802—reported relative gains of 12% and 21% over the best single-scale model.
watch_item: External validation and slide-level clinical evaluation are needed before translating patch-level results into practice.
paper_title: Multi-scale Fusion of Fast Vision Mamba and Foundation Model Features for Patch-Level Gleason Grading in Computational Pathology
